brief_summary: In the postmenopausal period, hormonal and physiological changes may be accompanied by alterations in body composition, physical performance, and body image. Psychosocial characteristics such as menopausal symptoms and self-esteem may also be associated with women's physical activity behaviors. During this period, physical activity levels are addressed within a multidimensional framework in which anthropometric, physical, and psychosocial factors are interrelated.
primary_outcomes: International Physical Activity Questionnaire Short Form (IPAQ-SF)
title: Determinants of Physical Activity in Postmenopausal Women

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical study aimed to compare microbial contamination of three different toothbrush types (standard plastic, silver nanoparticle, and bamboo charcoal) and to investigate whether storing toothbrushes in a bathroom or a room outside the bathroom affects microbial contamination.

The study included 72 healthy adolescents aged 11-18 years who were undergoing removable orthodontic appliance treatment. Participants were randomly assigned to one of three toothbrush groups and two storage conditions (bathroom or room). All participants received standardized oral hygiene instructions and used their assigned toothbrushes twice daily for one month.

After one month, the toothbrushes were collected and examined for the presence of three microorganisms: \*Streptococcus mutans\*, \*Lactobacillus\* spp., and \*Candida albicans\*. In addition, plaque index, gingival index, probing depth, and bleeding on probing were assessed at baseline and after one month.

The study was designed to determine whether toothbrushes marketed as having antimicrobial properties and different storage environments influence microbial contamination and short-term periodontal health.
primary_outcomes: Presence of Streptococcus mutans on Toothbrushes
Presence of Lactobacillus spp. on Toothbrushes
Presence of Candida albicans on Toothbrushes
title: Microbial Contamination of Different Toothbrush Types Stored in Bathrooms and Rooms in Adolescents

brief_summary:
The main purpose of this study is to compare two ways of giving the anti-cancer medicines abemaciclib and hormone therapy with tersolisib in participants with early breast cancer that has a genetic mutation (PIK3CA mutation).

For each participant, the study will last up to 56 weeks and include 12 visits.
primary_outcomes: Rate of Participants who Discontinue Tersolisib Due to Treatment Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs).
title: A Study of Tersolisib (LY4064809) and Abemaciclib With Hormone Therapies in Participants With PIK3CA-Mutated Early Breast Cancer

brief_summary: Obesity is associated with reduced physical fitness, functional limitations, and poorer quality of life (Kell et al., 2001). Nutritional support and supervised exercise can improve weight management and physical health, but low motivation and perceived lack of time often limit participation to physical activity (Alberga et al., 2013; Baillot et al., 2021). Evidence shows that shorter-time exercise strategies may help overcome these barriers and support training adherence (Poon et al., 2020). Brief activity bouts distributed throughout the day, including vigorous intermittent lifestyle physical activity and structured "exercise snacks," may help to improve cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle function, and metabolic health (Islam et al., 2022; Ahmadi et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024). Observational evidence also links VILPA to lower mortality risk (Stamatakis et al., 2023). Combining brief exercise bouts with education to interrupt prolonged sitting may therefore address both insufficient physical activity and sedentary behaviour (Dunstan et al., 2021; Dogra et al., 2022; Pinto et al., 2023). Generally, research has largely focused on healthy, inactive adults, with limited evidence in people with overweight or obesity (Jones et al., 2024). Rafiei et al. (2021) reported acute improvements in insulin and non-esterified fatty acid responses following brief stair-climbing bouts compared with prolonged sitting in adults with obesity. Schmidt et al. (2001) found comparable improvements in body composition and aerobic fitness following accumulated or continuous exercise during caloric restriction. The effects of exercise snacks combined with education to reduce sedentary behaviour nevertheless remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate the effects of an exercise-snacking programme on body composition, physical fitness, quality of life, and exercise adherence in adults with obesity.
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline fat mass at ten weeks
Change from baseline fat free mass at ten weeks
Change from baseline waist circumference at ten weeks
Change from baseline weight at ten weeks
title: Effects of "Exercise Snack" in Individuals With Obesity

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to determine the effectiveness of a low FODMAP diet and microencapsulated oral calcium butyrate supplementation in reducing GI symptoms among athletes in Perak.

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter, exploratory clinical study is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an all-oral combination of ivosidenib, sonrotoclax, and chidamide in adults with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) harboring an IDH1 R132 mutation.

Approximately 30 participants aged 18 years or older will be enrolled. Eligible participants must have previously untreated AML with a confirmed IDH1 R132 mutation and adequate heart, liver, and kidney function. Ivosidenib targets the abnormal IDH1 protein, sonrotoclax blocks BCL-2, a protein that helps leukemia cells survive, and chidamide affects gene regulation and may increase the sensitivity of leukemia cells to treatment. The study hypothesis is that combining these three medicines may produce deep and durable remissions with an acceptable safety profile while providing a treatment that can be taken entirely by mouth.

Treatment will be given in 28-day cycles. During induction treatment, all participants will receive oral ivosidenib, sonrotoclax, and chidamide. In the initial exploratory stage, participants will be assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three induction schedules. The schedules differ in the planned duration of sonrotoclax and chidamide treatment. A bone marrow examination will be performed on Day 10 or Day 14, depending on the assigned schedule, to determine whether sonrotoclax and/or chidamide should be continued through Day 28. Early remission results, adverse events, and overall tolerability will be reviewed to select a recommended induction schedule for the expansion stage.

Participants who achieve a response will receive at least three 28-day cycles of consolidation treatment with the three-drug combination. Treatment duration may be shortened or the next cycle may be delayed if blood cell counts recover slowly or other clinically important side effects occur. After consolidation, measurable residual disease (MRD) will be assessed. MRD refers to the small number of leukemia cells that may remain after treatment even when remission has been achieved. Participants who become negative for IDH1 MRD will proceed to maintenance treatment with oral ivosidenib for up to 2 years. Participants with persistent IDH1 MRD may receive additional consolidation treatment, and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may be considered according to the protocol and clinical assessment.

The primary outcome is the 1-year event-free survival rate, defined by whether participants remain alive without relapse or disease progression. Secondary outcomes include the composite complete remission rate after induction treatment, MRD clearance and the time to MRD clearance, relapse-free survival, overall survival, and exploratory biological markers. Safety will be evaluated by recording adverse events and monitoring blood counts, bone marrow findings, liver and kidney function, electrocardiograms, and other clinically indicated tests. Participants will be followed regularly during treatment and follow-up.
lead_sponsor: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University
title: An All-Oral Combination of Ivosidenib, Sonrotoclax, and Chidamide for Newly Diagnosed Acute Myeloid Leukemia With an IDH1 Mutation (ISC)

brief_summary:
Antenatal depression (AND) is a common mental health condition, affecting approximately 1 in 10 expectant mothers, yet many find it difficult to access the right kind of support. Feeling low during pregnancy can affect day-to-day wellbeing and is associated with difficulties in feeling connected to the unborn baby and to others around them. If left unsupported, AND can have wider consequences, including an increased risk of preterm birth, difficulties in the developing relationship between mother and baby, and effects on the child's development after birth.

Group singing may offer an accessible, non-clinical way to support mental health during pregnancy, providing a friendly, non-judgemental space in which to meet others and take part in a shared activity. This study builds on research from the Melodies for Mums programme, which showed that community group singing reduced symptoms of depression and improved the relationship between mothers and their babies after birth. This study aims to investigate whether a similar programme, Melodies for Mums to Be, delivered during pregnancy, can reduce symptoms of depression, improve mood and wellbeing, and support the relationship between expectant mothers and their unborn babies. The study is funded by the Psychiatry Research Trust and delivered by King's College London in partnership with Breathe Arts Health Research.

Fifty expectant mothers aged 18 or over who are experiencing symptoms of low mood (a score of 10 or above on the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) will be recruited from across London from 16 weeks' gestation. Participants will be randomly allocated either to attend a six-week group singing programme during pregnancy or to receive the same programme after the birth of their baby, ensuring that all participants have the opportunity to take part. Sessions will last approximately 60 minutes, be held weekly at community cultural venues across London, and be led by trained facilitators. No musical experience is needed.

Participants will complete questionnaires and interviews before, during, and after the programme, and at approximately 8 weeks, 7 months, and 12 months after giving birth. The main outcome is the change in depressive symptoms over the six-week programme period, compared between the two groups. Participants who consent will also provide saliva and blood samples to help understand whether singing during pregnancy is associated with changes in biological markers of stress and bonding.
primary_outcomes: Change in depressive symptoms (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, EPDS)
title: Melodies for Mums to Be: Community Group Singing Intervention for Pregnant Women With Antenatal Depressive Symptoms

brief_summary: This prospective, observational, single-center study aims to evaluate the predictive value of the Modified Frailty Index-5 (mFI-5) score on postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) admission requirements and 30-day mortality in geriatric patients undergoing hip fracture surgery. Patients aged 65 and older presenting with a hip fracture will be evaluated preoperatively using the mFI-5 scoring system (assessing diabetes, hypertension, COPD, congestive heart failure, and functional dependence). Intraoperative hemodynamic data, anesthesia type, and transfusion requirements will be documented. Postoperative ICU admission, total hospital stay, and 30-day survival status will be recorded to assess the prognostic capability of preoperative frailty levels.
interventions: Preoperative mFI-5 Assessment and Standard Surgical/Anesthetic Care
lead_sponsor: Dr Abdurrahman Yurtaslan Ankara Oncology Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Admission Rate
title: Geriatric Hip Fracture mFI-5 for Postoperative ICU Need and 30 Day Mortality

brief_summary:
Stroke is a leading cause of disability with over 1 million people in the UK living with the effects of stroke. Sleep is important for many aspects of daily life, but there is growing evidence that people sleep worse after a stroke, and this impacts negatively on rehabilitation outcomes and quality of life. Stroke survivors have highlighted to us that it is difficult to sleep in the hospital after a stroke, and they feel that sleep isn't perceived as high priority despite clear importance for next day function and healing.

This project will develop and test a sleep education package for clinical staff and stroke survivors in the rehabilitation hospital. Specifically, we aim to (1) develop a training programme for staff and a toolkit of resources about sleep for staff and stroke survivors, (2) assess acceptability and usability of the package, and, following modifications, (3) assess the feasibility of delivery of the sleep education package and collecting data about patient's sleep.
primary_outcomes: Staff perceptions of the usefulness of sleep education package
Staff perceptions of the relevance of the sleep education package
Staff perceptions of the appropriateness of the sleep education package
Patient perceptions of the usefulness of the sleep education package
title: Feasibility Of Sleep Treatment Education in Stroke Rehabilitation Settings

brief_summary:
Stroke is a major cause of disability and the second leading cause of death in adults. Some strokes are linked to atrial fibrillation (AF), a type of irregular heartbeat. When AF is found, doctors usually prescribe blood-thinning medicines to help prevent another stroke. If AF is not found, patients are usually treated with antiplatelet medicines, such as aspirin.

However, AF can be difficult to detect. Because of this, doctors may not know which treatment is best.

Our research team has developed computer programs that analyze a normal electrocardiogram (EKG) and predict whether a person may develop AF in the future. These programs have been shown to be highly accurate.

The goal of this study is to see how sharing these prediction results affects treatment decisions made by patients who have had an embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS) and their neurologist. An ESUS is a type of stroke where the exact cause cannot be identified.

Participants in the study will have their normal EKG analyzed using the prediction program. Researchers will then evaluate whether providing these results to the neurologist influences decisions about the patient's care.
primary_outcomes: Rates of Prescribing OAC versus Antiplatelet Agent
title: Impact of Atrial Fibrillation Prediction Model on Prescribing Oral Anti-Coagulation in Patients With Cryptogenic Stroke

brief_summary: This study investigates whether an eHealth cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) intervention for low self-esteem, SIYA-PT, is acceptable and feasible for an ethnically diverse population of emerging adults in Portugal.
title: SIYA-PT: An Internet-based CBT Intervention to Enhance Low Self-esteem Among Portuguese Emerging Adults

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether a novel integrated, multidisciplinary healthcare programme can improve quality of life for adults living with obesity on the island of Ireland.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does participation in the 52-week PEACETIME programme improve participants' quality of life?
* Does the programme improve clinical outcomes, including weight, blood glucose control, and other markers of health?
* Does the programme improve mental health, health empowerment, and self-management?
* Is the programme acceptable to patients and healthcare professionals, and is it cost-effective compared with standard practice?

Participants will receive a 52-week obesity management programme delivered by an interdisciplinary team comprising dietitians, psychologists, physiotherapists, physical activity specialists, nurses, and health coaches. Following a comprehensive assessment by the Multidisciplinary Team, participants will be allocated to one of four personalised care pathways based on their needs, goals, preferences, and clinical complexity: (1) digital health support with a Health Coach; (2) digital health support with additional Multidisciplinary Team input, including online group education and peer support; (3) a centre-based Multidisciplinary Team programme with face-to-face group education and individual support; or (4) a Clinical Psychology pathway including psychological assessment, group-based support, and individual interventions where required. All pathways include ongoing review, early assessment of progress, and maintenance support.

Participants will:

* Attend assessment appointments at the start of the programme (baseline), at approximately 24 weeks, and at 52 weeks.
* Have measurements taken, including weight, blood pressure, physical function, and blood tests where required.
* Complete questionnaires about quality of life, mental health, physical activity, health empowerment, and self-management.
* Receive personalised support through health coaching, group sessions, educational resources, and individual consultations, depending on their allocated pathway.
* Have access to a digital health platform for communication, education, monitoring progress, and attending online appointments where relevant to their pathway.
* Have relevant clinical information collected from their medical records to assess changes in health and healthcare use over time.

Researchers will compare participants' outcomes over the 52-week programme with their baseline measurements to assess changes in quality of life and other health outcomes. There is no comparison group within the main single-arm clinical programme.
title: Evaluation of a Novel Integrated Cross-border Clinical Healthcare Service Model to Increase Access to Care for People Living With Obesity

brief_summary: Women tend to manage emotional stress situations worse than men, which is reflected in their neurophysiological response at the brain level. Nervous system disorders have increased worldwide in recent years, affecting 40% of the total population, and their prevalence is higher in women, as well as the associated disability. According to the scientific literature, conscious and controlled rhythmic breathing at a slow pace influences cardiorespiratory parameters, cortical and subcortical areas of the brain and the activation of the parasympathetic branch of the autonomic nervous system (ANS). This has a positive effect not only on the nervous level, but also on motor activity, balance and cognitive efficiency, favouring the process of allostasis or the restoration of the state of organic equilibrium. This state of equilibrium is fundamental for functionality at both physiological and psychological levels, which clearly favors a state of health and well-being. However, recent systematic reviews report that passive recovery methods (i.e. breathing only) are less effective than combined methods (i.e. body-mind techniques such as Pilates or Yoga). However, within the combined group, they highlight the lack of control of the respiratory rhythm as a determining factor in the results. Moreover, its acute effect becomes important when it comes to recovering basal HRV to optimize daily organ function and, in turn, basal HRV is a determinant of the physiological response to a training stimulus. Therefore, the aim is to compare three Pilates-based interventions conducted with three different breathing rhythms (natural, fast, and slow) to determine their effectiveness on the autonomic nervous system and other psycho-physiological parameters.
title: Movement Controlled by Breath for Recovery

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, cross-sectional, observational study involving approximately 1,000 treatment-naive patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection at Beijing Ditan Hospital, Capital Medical University.

The study aims to investigate the relationship between HBV genetic characteristics, host molecular profiles, and clinical features of chronic HBV infection. Clinical and laboratory information, including liver function tests, HBV DNA levels, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels, and liver fibrosis assessments, will be collected from eligible participants.

Existing clinical data and stored serum samples will be used when authorized and approved by the Ethics Committee. Newly enrolled participants will contribute residual serum samples obtained after routine clinical testing. No additional blood collection or experimental treatment will be required for this study.

HBV whole-genome sequencing data will be analyzed to characterize viral genotypes, mutations, and viral diversity. In approximately 300 selected participants, serum metabolomics, quantitative proteomics, and immune-related factors will also be examined.

By integrating viral, metabolic, protein, immune, and clinical data, this study aims to identify molecular features and potential biomarkers associated with liver inflammation, early liver fibrosis, viral replication, and HBsAg expression. The findings may help improve understanding of differences among patients with chronic HBV infection and provide a basis for future research on risk assessment and disease management.
primary_outcomes: Serum ALT Level by HBV Genomic Characteristic Group
title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis of Treatment-Naive Patients With Chronic HBV Infection

brief_summary:
This study is a partially blinded (outcome assessors and data analysts) and parallel-group randomized controlled trial. Community-dwelling people aged ≥65 years who have not received the SIV for the approaching flu season will be randomized evenly (1:1) into either the intervention group or the control group. During the intervention period, the intervention group will have access to the hybrid combination of a rule-based chatbot (SIV-Chatbot) with the ChatGPT-supported real-time Question \& Answer (QA) functions, while the control group will have access only to the SIV-Chatbot.

The SIV-Chatbot will deliver the same interventions for both groups. The number of intervention sessions (four) and timing (week 0, 2, 4 \& 6) will also be the same. In the intervention group, the hybrid Chatbot will invite the participants to raise open-ended questions related to SIV using flexible methods (such as voice messages, typing with keyboards, or handwriting) at each session. The ChatGPT will answer these questions immediately in the format of text messages. The functions can be used repeatedly throughout the intervention period (weeks 0-6), and participants will be free to spend as much time as they want on such functions.

Telephone interviews will be conducted at baseline (T0), after completion of the intervention (T1), and six months after T1 (T2). The primary outcome will be the self-reported SIV uptake measured at T2. The research team will validate that outcome by requesting the participants upload an image of their SIV receipt, while hiding their personal identification, via the WhatsApp account used in this study.
title: Combining an Effective Rule-based Chatbot With ChatGPT-supported Real-time Question-answer Functions to Promote Seasonal Influenza Vaccination Among Community-dwelling People Aged 65 Years and Above

brief_summary:
This study will test whether adding walking practice to standard rehabilitation improves balance while walking after lower back surgery. The study will include 60 adults aged 30 to 65 who still have difficulty walking or keeping their balance after surgery to relieve pressure on the nerves in the lower back caused by a narrowing of the spinal canal.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups. One group will receive standard rehabilitation. The other group will receive the same rehabilitation plus extra practice with everyday walking tasks, such as changing speed, turning, and stepping over obstacles. Both groups will attend three supervised sessions per week for eight weeks.

Participants will be assessed before starting the program and again at weeks 4 and 8. The person who performs the assessments will be unaware of each participant's group assignment. The main outcome is balance during walking tasks at week 8. The study will also assess walking speed and distance, the ability to get up from a chair and move around, back and leg pain, and how back problems affect daily activities.
primary_outcomes: Functional Gait Assessment (FGA) Total Score at Week 8
title: Walking Training After Lumbar Decompression Surgery

brief_summary: This study examined whether a structured teaching program that combines three-dimensional reconstruction of kidney cases with generative artificial intelligence dialogue helps undergraduate medical students learn during their urology clerkship. One hundred and eighty students took part between September 2024 and January 2025. Students who received the combined program were compared with students who received conventional multimedia teaching. Both groups completed knowledge and clinical reasoning tests before and after teaching, and students in the combined group also completed satisfaction questionnaires. The study was registered after the teaching period had ended.
interventions: Structured 3D reconstruction and generative AI program
title: 3D Reconstruction and Generative AI in Undergraduate Urology Clerkship

brief_summary: The goal of this interventional study is to test whether short videos of electronic-cigarette (e-cigarette) counter-marketing lessons work to decrease people's intent to use and smoke e-cigarettes. Using short videos, the investigators hope to inform participants about the marketing strategies that e-cigarette companies use to try to get people to purchase and use e-cigarettes. The investigators hope to find that, after watching the short videos, people will be able to point out when e-cigarette companies are trying to sell their products, and hopefully they will have a lower interest in buying and using e-cigarettes. The investigators also hope participants will learn more about the addictiveness and harmfulness of using e-cigarettes by watching the short videos.
primary_outcomes: Susceptibility to use e-cigarettes among those who never used
title: Understanding Vape Counter-Marketing Study

brief_summary: This study will test how a new blood test for troponin T can be introduced into routine hospital care in Denmark and Norway. The study will look at whether the new test helps doctors assess and treat patients with possible heart problems more effectively and safely.
interventions: Use of the 6th generation of cardiac troponin T assay
Standard arm (5th generation of troponin T)
primary_outcomes: Composite endpoint of death from any cause and MI, or revascularization within 6 months after admission (PCI and CABG).
title: Implementing the 6th Generation Cardiac Troponin T

brief_summary:
This is a single-centre, observational retrospective and prospective study aimed at evaluating the clinical and functional outcomes of patients who underwent combined anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and posterolateral corner (PLC) reconstruction using the Over-The-Top (OTT) technique.

The primary outcome is the improvement in knee function, assessed using the Lysholm Knee Score by comparing pre-injury/preoperative status with postoperative follow-up. Secondary outcomes include knee stability, assessed through clinical examinations and instrumental measurements (KT-1000, KiRA, PIVOT App and Telos stress radiographs), return to sport, pain, MRI findings and postoperative complications.

Patients aged 18-65 years with a minimum follow-up of 24 months will be included. The study aims to provide evidence on the effectiveness of the combined ACL and PLC reconstruction using the OTT technique.
title: Clinical and Instrumental Assessment and Evaluation of Return to Sport in Patients Who Underwent Surgical Treatment for Posterolateral Corner (PLC) Injuries Associated With Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Injuries.

brief_summary: The objective of this randomized clinical trial is to evaluate and compare the effect of four different residual adhesive removal techniques following orthodontic bracket debonding on postoperative tooth hypersensitivity. The study compares low-speed tungsten carbide burs against fiberglass burs, white stone burs, and rubber-impregnated polishing points. Postoperative hypersensitivity will be evaluated using a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) with an air-blast stimulus test immediately after debonding, at 24 hours, and at 7 days follow-up.
title: Effect of Different Adhesive Removal Techniques After Orthodontic Bracket Debonding on Postoperative Hypersensitivity: A Randomized Clinical Trial

brief_summary: This community-based observational study primarily aims to estimate the prevalence, characterize the clinical spectrum, and identify associated risk factors for moderate or greater valvular heart disease (VHD) in China. Longitudinal follow-up will characterize VHD progression and assess long-term clinical outcomes among participants.
primary_outcomes: Moderate or greater valvular heart disease
title: Prevalence, Risk Factors, and Clinical Outcomes of Valvular Heart Disease

brief_summary: This prospective observational cohort study evaluates changes in high-frequency skin ultrasound findings in patients with cutaneous leishmaniasis receiving routine clinical treatment at the University Hospital of Brasilia, Brazil. The primary outcome is clinical cure assessed three months after completion of treatment. Ultrasonography will characterize dermal and hypodermal thickness, echogenicity and color Doppler vascular signals over repeated examinations. Associations of baseline clinical, histopathological, and ultrasound findings with healing will be investigated. Participants will be followed for 12 months from treatment initiation to evaluate their clinical course, including relapse.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Clinical Cure
title: High-Frequency Ultrasound Monitoring of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis During Treatment

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-center, exploratory clinical study designed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and clinical utility of \^68Ga-grazytracer positron emission tomography (PET) for noninvasive in vivo visualization of immune cell effector function in patients with cancer and autoimmune diseases. \^68Ga-grazytracer is a granzyme B (GZMB)-targeted PET radiotracer developed to visualize cytotoxic immune activation.

Approximately 60-80 adult participants will be enrolled in two study cohorts: (1) patients with malignant tumors who are scheduled to receive systemic anticancer therapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, CAR-T cell therapy, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, or combination therapy; and (2) patients with autoimmune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, and immune myocarditis, who are receiving or planning to receive immunomodulatory treatment.

Participants will undergo \^68Ga-grazytracer PET/CT imaging before treatment initiation and again during the predefined treatment period. Imaging findings, including tracer uptake and semiquantitative parameters (e.g., SUVmax and target-to-background ratio), will be analyzed together with clinical outcomes, laboratory findings, disease activity assessments, and follow-up data.

The primary objectives are to evaluate the safety and tolerability of \^68Ga-grazytracer PET imaging and to investigate the association between GZMB-targeted PET imaging and treatment response in patients with cancer, disease activity and organ involvement in autoimmune diseases, and therapeutic response to immunomodulatory treatment. This study aims to provide preliminary evidence supporting the use of \^68Ga-grazytracer PET as a molecular imaging biomarker for noninvasive assessment of immune effector function in cancer and autoimmune diseases.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Adverse Events Related to ⁶⁸Ga-grazytracer PET/CT Imaging
Change in Maximum Standardized Uptake Value (SUVmax) on ⁶⁸Ga-grazytracer PET
Change in Target-to-Background Ratio (TBR) on ⁶⁸Ga-grazytracer PET
title: ^68Ga-grazytracer PET for In Vivo Visualization of Immune Cell Effector Functions

brief_summary: Infants with Down syndrome (DS) exhibit early developmental delays in motor skills and multiple other domains. Once infants are upright and moving, they have new opportunities for exploring the environment and interacting with objects and people that are important for early learning and development. This project will allow the investigators to assess the feasibility of a home-based mobility and play intervention for infants with DS (using a body weight supported harness system- Portable Mobility Use Aid (PUMA) for Children and characterize its impact on promoting mobility, exploration, and play with objects and caregivers. PUMA is a specialized pediatric partial body-weight support system designed to give children with developmental delays or physical disabilities the upright support they need to move, explore, and play independently.
title: Creating Mobility-supported Home Play Environments to Enhance Development in Infants With Down Syndrome

brief_summary:
ACTs could be used as first-line treatment for Plasmodium falciparum malaria without clinical signs of severity but with biological severity criteria.

The study aims to determine the real-world frequency of ACT monotherapy use in cases of P. falciparum malaria with severity criteria, and to compare the treatment success of ACTs with that of artesunate.
primary_outcomes: Measure: Frequency of ACT monotherapy use in patients with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
title: Management of Severe Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria With Oral Artemisinin Derivatives

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of dual-effect myopia control spectacle lenses in slowing myopia progression compared with Nikon MyoEase 2.0 lenses in children aged 8-13 years.

This is a single-center, randomized, open-label, parallel-group, noninferiority clinical trial. A total of 194 children with myopia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to wear either dual-effect myopia control spectacle lenses or Nikon MyoEase 2.0 lenses for 12 months.

The primary outcome is the change in cycloplegic objective spherical equivalent refraction from baseline to 12 months. Secondary outcomes include changes in refractive error, ocular biometric parameters, visual acuity, binocular visual function, and visual questionnaire scores. Safety will also be assessed throughout the study.
lead_sponsor: Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Sun Yat-sen University
primary_outcomes: Change in Cycloplegic Spherical Equivalent Refraction at 12 Months
title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual-Effect Myopia Control Lenses for Slowing Myopia Progression: A Single-Center, Randomized, Controlled, Noninferiority Trial

brief_summary:
Preterm birth is an important cause of illness and death in newborns. Changes in the normal bacteria in the vagina may increase vaginal pH and may be associated with preterm labor. Lactobacillus acidophilus combined with ultra-low-dose estriol may help restore the normal vaginal environment and lower vaginal pH.

The purpose of this study is to compare two treatment durations, 6 days and 12 days, of vaginal tablets containing Lactobacillus acidophilus and ultra-low-dose estriol in pregnant women with threatened preterm labor and a vaginal pH greater than 4.5.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive one vaginal tablet once daily for either 6 days or 12 days. Vaginal pH will be assessed before treatment and on Days 7, 14, and 21. The main outcome is the change in vaginal pH from before treatment to Day 14. The study will also evaluate the proportion of participants whose vaginal pH returns to the normal range, whether the effect is maintained after treatment, treatment-related adverse events, and hospital readmission within 30 days.
lead_sponsor: Queen Savang Vadhana Memorial Hospital, Thailand
primary_outcomes: Change in Vaginal pH From Baseline to Day 14
title: Vaginal Flora Modulation With Lactobacillus and Estriol in Threatened Preterm Labor

The study consists of three parts: Part A (Single-Dose Escalation Study), Part B (Food Effect and Metabolite Study), and Part C (Multiple-Dose Escalation Study).

brief_summary:
This clinical study examined a structured expressive arts program designed for students preparing for university entrance examinations. The objective of the study was to determine whether this program could reduce test anxiety. Additionally, the study investigated the students' level of "academic self-efficacy"-their confidence in their own ability to perform academic tasks.

The primary research questions were as follows:

* Did students who participated in the program report lower levels of test anxiety compared to students who received only the standard services offered at the school?
* Did students who participated in the program report higher levels of academic self-efficacy compared to students who received only the standard services offered at the school?

The study involved 60 eleventh-grade students, aged 15-17, attending a science high school in the Bafra district of Samsun, Türkiye. Participation was voluntary, and both the students and their parents provided written informed consent prior to the study. Before being assigned to groups, all students completed a set of questionnaires. An independent statistician then divided the students into two groups of 30 using computer-generated random numbers. One group participated in the arts program, while the comparison group continued with their regular classes and standard school guidance services. The program was conducted within the school setting over a period of five weeks. Each week, students attended a group session lasting approximately 90 minutes. These sessions were facilitated by a researcher trained in arts-based psychosocial support. Each session consisted of an opening activity, a brief introduction to the topic, art-based activities, a discussion segment, and a closing activity. The program combined expressive art methods with the principles of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Students explored the connections between thoughts, emotions, bodily reactions, and behaviors. They practiced recognizing maladaptive thoughts regarding exams and developing more balanced alternatives to replace them. Activities such as drawing, collage-making, the use of colors and symbols, and guided imagery offered students various ways to express their experiences.The five sessions covered the following topics:

Recognizing test anxiety: Students illustrated their anxiety, addressing the concerns, emotions, and physical reactions they associate with examinations.

Examining self-critical thoughts: Through art, students gave form to their "inner critic." They questioned discouraging thoughts and developed more realistic, supportive statements.

Identifying personal strengths: Students envisioned and depicted themselves coping with an exam, evaluating the strengths and resources they could draw upon when facing academic challenges.

Recalling past achievements: Students created a collage reflecting their previous successes and the challenges they had overcome, while reflecting on the efforts, strategies, and support that contributed to these outcomes.

Preparing for exam day: Students imagined themselves in an examination setting and illustrated the use of effective coping strategies. They practiced how to respond to difficult questions and how to refocus their attention on the task at hand.

The art activities focused on personal expression and self-assessment; students were not graded on their artistic skills or the visual quality of their work. They were free to choose whether or not to share their creations with the group and were encouraged to explain the meanings behind their own drawings and collages. Throughout the study, the comparison group continued to receive standard educational and school-based guidance services. Both groups completed the same outcome questionnaires during the same assessment period. Researchers measured test anxiety and academic self-efficacy both before the program and in the week following its conclusion. The test anxiety questionnaire covered worry, difficulty concentrating, tension, and the physical symptoms of anxiety. The academic self-efficacy questionnaire, meanwhile, assessed self-confidence regarding one's ability to handle academic tasks. Lower test anxiety scores indicated less anxiety, while higher academic self-efficacy scores indicated greater self-confidence. The researchers compared how the questionnaire scores changed across the two groups, examining general test anxiety, various dimensions of anxiety, and academic self-efficacy. The primary comparison focused on differences between the groups in terms of changes observed before and after the program. The study evaluated the short-term effects of the holistic program within the school environment; it did not include subsequent follow-up assessments.
interventions: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy-Based Structured Expressive Arts Therapy
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Multidimensional Test Anxiety Scale Total Score
Change From Baseline in Academic Self-Efficacy Scale Total Score
title: Effects of a Structured Expressive Arts Program Based on Cognitive Behavioral Therapy on Test Anxiety and Academic Self-Efficacy (Confidence in Academic Tasks) in Eleventh-Grade High School Students: A Randomized Controlled Study

The purpose of this study is to learn whether tighter control of blood sugar, when combined with the drug brolucizumab, can help people with diabetic macular edema (DME) see better than standard blood sugar care combined with the same drug.

DME is a swelling in the back of the eye that can blur vision. It happens in some people with diabetes. Brolucizumab is an injection into the eye that treats this swelling. Many people improve with this injection, but some do not improve as much as hoped. Researchers think that keeping blood sugar closer to normal may help the eye injection work better.

This study will randomly assign participants to one of two groups. One group will receive intensive blood sugar management, which includes wearing a small sensor that checks sugar levels throughout the day and more frequent check-ins with a diabetes care team. The other group will receive standard blood sugar care. Both groups will receive brolucizumab eye injections on the same schedule.

Researchers will compare how much vision changes in each group over about 6 months. They will also check the amount of swelling in the eye and monitor safety.

This study is for adults with DME who are planning to start brolucizumab treatment. Participants will be in the study for about 6 months and will visit the clinic regularly for eye exams, injections, and blood tests.

CAR T-cell therapy is a treatment that uses a patient's own immune cells to fight cancer. However, some patients relapse (the cancer comes back) after CAR T-cell therapy. This study will test whether taking two drugs - chidamide (a tablet taken by mouth) and a PD-1 inhibitor (given by intravenous infusion) - as maintenance therapy after CAR T-cell therapy can help keep the cancer from coming back.

Participants in this study will receive CAR T-cell therapy, followed by maintenance treatment with chidamide combined with a PD-1 inhibitor. Doctors will closely monitor participants for how well the treatment works and for any side effects. The study will take place at a single hospital, and all participants will receive the same treatment.

The main goal of the study is to find out if this maintenance treatment is effective and safe for patients with TP53-mutant large B-cell lymphoma.

Both programs lasted four weeks and included the same planned amount of classroom and simulation teaching. Clinical learning took place within routine supervised residency activities. The study did not assign surgical treatment to patients or change patient care for research purposes.

Residents completed assessments before training, shortly after training, and approximately eight weeks after the post-training assessment. Reviewers who did not know the assigned group assessed recorded simulation performance. The study also assessed procedural knowledge, technical errors during simulation, skill retention, and residents' learning experience.

brief_summary:
Despite its low incidence, pediatric cardiopulmonary arrest remains associated with high mortality and morbidity. The adequate preparation and administration of drugs can impact favourably on the outcomes of cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

Nursing staff rely on cognitive aids such as paper support, calculators, or spreadsheets to ensure correct drug administration.

Numerous strategies have been proposed to prevent medication errors, including the emergence of mHealth.

This study evaluates the efficacy and usefulness of the PEDIDOSIS smartphone application (app) for nursing staff in a simulated pediatric emergency setting. A multicentre high-fidelity simulation-based randomized controlled trial was conducted in a pediatric emergency setting with nursing professionals from different hospitals in Spain. Randomisation groups: PEDIDOSIS app (La Paz Hospital, Spain) vs. conventional methods (such as printed or electronic medication tables, smartphones, calculators or no cognitive aid). To avoid bias due to differences in pediatric emergency experience, each group was randomly assigned the same number of participants with experience (\> 5 years) and without experience (≤ 5 years). Epinephrine, bicarbonate, midazolam, and norepinephrine on two ocassions were administered in a simulation scenario. Number and magnitude of medication errors, time taken to drug administration were evaluated as measured with video recording; stress, satisfaction, and usability as measured using standardized survey tools were evaluated.

One-hundred and five nurses participated. The incidence of wrong dose administration by any deviation from the correct dose was 51.5% for the control group vs. 26.4% for the PEDIDOSIS app group (p \< 0.001). The OR for a wrong dose administration \> 10% deviation with PEDIDOSIS app vs. conventional methods was 0.24 \[0.14-0.4\]), with a risk difference of 20.7%. The proportion of participants committing several medication errors (ME) was substantially lower with the app (15.1%) than with conventional methods (57.7%). Overall satisfaction regarding drug preparation was higher and stress lower in the app group. The System Usability Scale (SUS) score obtained for PEDIDOSIS app was 78.9 out of 100.
title: Evaluating PEDIDOSIS App in Pediatric CPR Simulations

brief_summary:
Background Perianal fistulae are among the most disabling complications of Crohn's disease, causing significant morbidity, impaired quality of life, and substantial healthcare utilisation. Despite advances in biologic and surgical therapies, many patients experience persistent fistula drainage and fail to achieve durable healing.

Tissue hypoxia is a key regulator of intestinal inflammation and impaired wound healing in inflammatory bowel disease. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) increases tissue oxygenation, promotes angiogenesis, modulates inflammatory pathways, and may enhance fistula healing.

Preliminary studies suggest that HBOT is a safe and effective adjunctive treatment for refractory perianal Crohn's fistulae, with reported clinical response rates of 75-87% and remission rates of 50-60%. However, current evidence is limited by small sample sizes and the absence of prospective studies within UK clinical practice.

Aim To evaluate the preliminary efficacy of HBOT in patients with refractory perianal Crohn's fistulae treated in an outpatient setting.

Methods This prospective pilot study will recruit ten adults with refractory perianal Crohn's fistulae from the Inflammatory Bowel Disease service at Barts Health NHS Trust. Refractory disease will be defined as persistent fistula drainage or failure to heal despite optimised medical therapy and appropriate surgical management. Participants will undergo HBOT 100% oxygen at 2.4 ATA for approximately 90 minutes per session, 40 sessions over 8 weeks. The primary outcome will be overall clinical response, defined as either clinical remission (complete cessation of fistula drainage) or partial response (clinically meaningful reduction in drainage and symptoms). Secondary outcomes will include treatment adherence, safety, tolerability, patient acceptability, and feasibility of recruitment and study completion.

Expected Impact This pilot study will generate preliminary efficacy and feasibility data to inform the design, outcome measures, and sample size calculations of a larger clinical trial evaluating HBOT as a novel treatment strategy for refractory perianal Crohn's disease in the United Kingdom.
primary_outcomes: Clinical Response of Perianal Crohn's Disease Fistulae
title: HBOT for Perianal Crohn's Disease

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to compare two surgical approaches for correcting drooping of the upper eyelid (aponeurotic ptosis) in adults who need surgery. This condition occurs when the tissue connecting the eyelid-lifting muscle to the eyelid becomes weakened or detached. It can affect one or both eyes.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does surgery performed through the inner surface of the eyelid (posterior approach) achieve an upper eyelid height at 6 months that is not meaningfully worse than surgery performed through the skin (anterior approach)?
* How do the two approaches compare in terms of complications, operating time, swelling, bruising, eyelid appearance, and patient satisfaction?
* How stable are the results during the 6 months after surgery?

Researchers will compare anterior and posterior approaches to levator aponeurosis advancement, a procedure that repositions and reattaches the tissue connecting the eyelid-lifting muscle to the eyelid. Both approaches are routinely used at Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre in Madrid, Spain, where the study will take place.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of the two surgical groups, with an equal chance of receiving either approach. All procedures will be performed under local anesthesia by the same experienced surgeon.

The main outcome is upper eyelid height 6 months after surgery, measured as the distance between the upper eyelid edge and the reflection of a light at the center of the pupil. The study will assess whether the posterior approach is no more than 0.5 millimeters worse than the anterior approach for this measurement. An independent healthcare professional will measure eyelid height and assess eyelid appearance.

Participants will:

* Attend a preoperative assessment, including an eye examination and measurements of eyelid position and movement.
* Undergo surgery using the randomly assigned approach.
* Attend follow-up visits the day after surgery, at 1 week, and at 1, 3, and 6 months.
* Have eyelid measurements and standardized photographs taken, and be assessed for swelling, bruising, and complications.
* Answer questions about their satisfaction with the appearance and function of their eyelids at 1, 3, and 6 months.

The visits and clinical assessments follow the hospital's usual care schedule for this surgery. Participation does not require additional visits or invasive tests beyond routine care.
primary_outcomes: Margin Reflex Distance 1 (MRD1) at 6 Months After Surgery
title: Anterior Versus Posterior Surgery for Eyelid Ptosis

* Does the infection return after treatment?

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of three groups:

The matching creams contain no active study ingredient and help keep treatment assignments hidden. Participants and the researchers assessing their skin will not know which treatment each participant receives.

Participants will apply their assigned creams twice daily for four weeks. They will attend study visits for skin examinations, symptom assessments, and monitoring for side effects. Skin scrapings will be examined to check whether the infection has cleared. This study aimed to evaluate changes in quality of life and uremic toxin levels after switching from conventional hemodialysis to HDx. Patients who had been receiving maintenance hemodialysis for at least 10 years underwent HDx for three months. Quality of life and blood levels of selected uremic toxins were assessed before and after the treatment period.

The study aimed to determine whether switching to HDx was associated with changes in patients' quality of life and uremic toxin profiles.

VR is a computer-generated 3D environment that people can interact with. The study looks at what staff members know about VR, whether they have used it, and what they think about using it in teaching. It also looks at what may prevent its use in dental education. Participants complete one anonymous online questionnaire. The results may help guide staff training and teaching plans in dental schools.

brief_summary:
Primary dysmenorrhea is a common condition characterized by recurrent menstrual pain in the absence of identifiable pelvic pathology. Menstrual pain may be accompanied by changes in posture, neuromuscular function, and postural control. These changes may influence how body weight is distributed across the feet during standing.

The purpose of this observational study is to investigate the association between primary dysmenorrhea severity and plantar pressure distribution in post-pubertal females.

The study will include 79 female university students aged 18-23 years with a history of primary dysmenorrhea. Participants will be recruited from the first through fourth academic years of the Faculty of Physical Therapy at Al Hayat University in Cairo, Egypt.

Each participant will undergo a single assessment during the menstrual phase, specifically within the first three days of menstruation.

Primary dysmenorrhea severity will be assessed using the Working Ability, Location, Intensity, Days of Pain, Dysmenorrhea (WaLIDD) scale. The scale produces a total score ranging from 0 to 12, with higher scores indicating greater severity.

Plantar pressure distribution will be assessed using the DIERS pedoscan system during standardized barefoot quiet standing. The assessment will include plantar pressure distribution and anterior-posterior and right-left weight distribution.

A minimum of two valid 30-second standing measurements will be obtained and averaged for analysis.

The study will examine whether greater primary dysmenorrhea severity is associated with measurable differences in plantar pressure distribution and weight-bearing characteristics.

No therapeutic intervention, randomization, or experimental treatment allocation will be performed.
primary_outcomes: Primary Dysmenorrhea Severity Assessed by WaLIDD Score
title: Association Between Menstrual Pain Severity and Plantar Pressure in Young Women

brief_summary: The study will investigate gait stability in individuals post-stroke compared with age- and sex-matched healthy adults. Participants will undergo laboratory-based walking assessments under different environmental conditions, including level walking, uphill and downhill walking, and unexpected slip perturbations, with and without added cognitive, postural, and load-carrying tasks. The primary outcome measures will be the Margin of Stability (MOS), step width, and step width variability.

brief_summary:
Our study aims to investigate the impact of virtual reality headset use on pain, anxiety, and vital signs in pregnant women after they receive a vaccine. Pain and anxiety will be assessed using relevant scales, while vital signs-specifically blood pressure, pulse, and oxygen saturation-will be measured using a blood pressure monitor and a pulse oximeter.

The study is conducted at the Afyonkarahisar Family Health Centre No. 6-the facility where the researcher is employed-between December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026. This location was selected to facilitate access to the target group, ensure an efficient and reliable data collection process, and enhance the overall feasibility of the research.

The study population will consist of pregnant women who visit the Family Health Centre for pregnancy follow-ups or vaccinations during the specified study period. The research will involve two groups: one control group (Group 1) and one intervention group (Group 2).

Given the interventional nature of this study-and noting that no existing literature could be found examining the effects of virtual reality (VR) headsets on anxiety, pain, or vital signs in pregnant women undergoing vaccination-a pilot study involving at least 30 participants will be conducted first. Subsequently, a power analysis will be performed using the G\*Power 3.1 software to determine the final sample size. The projected sample size is 100 participants for Group 1 and 100 for Group 2, totalling 200 participants.

Assignment to the intervention and control groups will take place when pregnant women who meet the inclusion criteria arrive at Family Health Centre No. 06. A sealed-envelope method will be used to ensure randomisation when allocating the pregnant women into the intervention and control groups. Envelopes will contain slips of paper marked with either an odd or an even number. Those who select an odd number will be assigned to the control group (Group 1), while those who select an even number will be assigned to the intervention group (Group 2).

A single-blind approach will be employed, in which the individuals responsible for entering data into the SPSS software and those conducting the statistical analyses will be blinded. Data entry will be performed by individuals who have no knowledge of the study groups, and statistical analyses will be conducted by a statistician who is also unaware of the study groups.

Data for the study will be collected using a sociodemographic characteristics form, a pre-vaccination pregnancy monitoring form, and a post-vaccination pregnancy monitoring form.

All pregnant women arriving for vaccination who meet the inclusion criteria will be provided with information about the study, after which they will complete a sociodemographic characteristics form. Subsequently, participants will be randomised into groups using an envelope method.

Group 1 (Control Group) will not watch a pre-vaccination video via virtual reality (VR) headsets; however, data will be collected using a pre-vaccination monitoring form (before the vaccination) and a post-vaccination monitoring form (after the vaccination).

Group 2 (Experimental Group) will first complete the pre-vaccination monitoring form, followed by a 5-minute video session using VR headsets. The vaccination will be administered after the video, and data will be collected 5 minutes post-vaccination using the post-vaccination monitoring form.

Since the virtual reality intervention in our study is specific to the pre-vaccination period, applying it to the control group at a later stage would not be methodologically appropriate.

In this study, the administration of the virtual reality intervention, the recording of vital signs, and the completion of the forms will be carried out by the researcher.
title: Virtual Reality Headset Intervention on Pain, Anxiety, and Vital Signs in Pregnant Women Following Vaccination

brief_summary:

Colonoscopy performance is important because colonoscopies are how doctors detect and remove pre-cancerous polyps. The participants in this study are doctors, usually surgeons, who perform some colonoscopies as part of their practice. These doctors usually do not receive feedback on their performance, and therefore lack information on how to potentially improve their ability to detect and remove pre-cancerous polyps.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

2. Does customizing the report card lead to better acceptance of the information shared?

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if leg position-sense training helps men after a stroke. It includes men aged 50 to 65 whose stroke happened 6 months to 2 years ago. Position sense, also called proprioception, is the body's ability to feel where the legs are without looking.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does this training improve trunk control (the ability to keep the upper body steady and upright)? Does this training help participants stand up from a chair faster and more easily?

Researchers will compare standard physical therapy alone to standard physical therapy plus leg position-sense training. They want to see if the added training works better.

Participants will:

Attend 60-minute physical therapy sessions 3 times a week for 6 weeks Do standard leg exercises, stretching, and walking practice In the training group, also do 9 balance exercises, such as standing on one leg, stepping onto a step, and shifting weight on a balance board Take tests of trunk control, leg movement, and standing up from a chair 5 times, before and after the 6 weeks Be video recorded from the side while standing up and sitting down

Clinical validation will be performed by comparing PBPK-predicted plasma mirtazapine concentrations with observed concentrations obtained from healthy Vietnamese volunteers. Pharmacokinetic data from a bioequivalence (BE) study of mirtazapine will be used as supplementary data to support model validation.

PBPK simulations will be conducted to investigate the effects of physiological and metabolic variability on mirtazapine exposure. The findings are expected to improve understanding of interindividual pharmacokinetic variability and provide a scientific foundation for future individualized mirtazapine therapy.

brief_summary:
The COMPAZzz project aims to co-develop and evaluate the feasibility of a blended pain and sleep management intervention for adolescents and young adults (AYA) living beyond cancer. Pain and sleep disturbances are common among AYA living beyond cancer and frequently coexist, whereby pain may disrupt sleep and poor sleep may increase pain. In turn, these symptoms may negatively affect quality of life, psychological well-being, and participation in education, work, and social activities.

Despite the considerable impact of these symptoms, pain and sleep disturbances are often addressed separately in survivorship care. COMPAZzz seeks to address this gap by developing an integrated, non-pharmacological (= without administering medication) intervention combining principles of Pain Science Education (PSE) and Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for insomnia (= sleeplessness) (CBT-i). PSE aims to improve understanding of pain by addressing misconceptions and explaining the biological, psychological, and social factors that influence pain experiences. CBT-i targets thoughts, behaviours, and emotions that contribute to sleep disturbances.

Using a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach, AYA living beyond cancer will actively contribute to the development of the intervention in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, including significant others and oncology clinicians. This collaborative approach aims to ensure that the intervention reflects the needs, preferences, and lived experiences of the target population, thereby supporting its acceptability, engagement, and potential implementation in clinical practice and everyday life.

COMPAZzz aims to establish a foundation for more integrated and person-centered survivorship care addressing co-occurring pain and sleep disturbances in AYA living beyond cancer.

brief_summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a highly prevalent malignancy worldwide. Although radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is widely used for the treatment of early-stage small HCC, its 5-year recurrence rate reaches up to 70%, significantly higher than that of surgical resection, suggesting that the tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a critical role in the progression of residual tumors. Notably, in the context of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), HCC patients with concurrent fatty liver have an even higher risk of post-RFA recurrence and metastasis, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Recent studies have shown that extracellular vesicles (EVs), as important mediators of intercellular communication, are abundantly released in the fatty liver microenvironment. By carrying bioactive molecules such as proteins and nucleic acids, EVs remodel the TME and promote HCC cell proliferation, migration, and immune evasion. However, how fatty liver-derived EVs specifically regulate the malignant progression of residual tumors and reshape the immune and metabolic microenvironment under conditions of local thermal stress and ischemia-hypoxia following RFA remains poorly understood. Based on these findings, this project proposes the scientific hypothesis that abnormally released EVs in the fatty liver microenvironment promote post-RFA tumor progression by remodeling the TME and inducing residual HCC cells to acquire a more aggressive phenotype. Elucidating this mechanism is of great significance for understanding the causes of high post-RFA recurrence in the context of fatty liver, identifying potential biomarkers, and developing novel adjuvant therapeutic strategies.
lead_sponsor: The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University School of Medicine
title: Liver Tumor Microenvironment Remodeling Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression

The findings will be compared with those of previous studies and with our institutional data on patients with stage IV NSCLC who received concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy for 2-4 cycles and then 2 years of PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy. This comparison may demonstrate that, after concurrent chemoradiotherapy for stage IV NSCLC, ivonescimab plus chemotherapy for 2-4 cycles followed by 2 years of ivonescimab maintenance therapy achieves superior efficacy compared with PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy for 2-4 cycles followed by 2 years of PD-1 inhibitor maintenance therapy, with a comparable toxicity profile.
interventions: Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy followed by 2-year ivonescimab maintenance after concurrent chemoradiotherapy in stage IV non-small cell lung cancer

brief_summary:
Open fractures of the tibia are at risk of infection because the injury damages the surrounding soft tissues. This study will compare the frequency of postoperative infection in patients with Gustilo-Anderson type I and II open tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary interlocking nail (ILN) fixation or plate fixation after three days of intravenous prophylactic antibiotic therapy.

A total of 170 patients aged 18-60 years will be included and randomly allocated into two groups of 85 patients each. Group A will undergo ILN fixation, while Group B will undergo plate fixation. Patients will be monitored for signs of infection, including pain, redness, swelling, and wound discharge, during hospital stay and follow-up. The main outcome will be the presence of postoperative infection within three months of surgery.

The findings may help clinicians compare infection rates between these two fixation methods in open tibial shaft fractures.
title: Infection Rate With Intramedullary Interlocking Nail Versus Plate Fixation in Open Tibial Fractures

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-arm, open-label Phase II clinical study. The main purpose of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of nab-paclitaxel combined with retlirafusp alfa injection and apatinib mesylate in patients with advanced mucosal melanoma.

Participants will receive treatment with nab-paclitaxel combined with retlirafusp alfa injection and apatinib mesylate. Each treatment cycle lasts 3 weeks, and participants will receive a total of 6 cycles. Participants whose disease does not progress after the initial treatment will continue maintenance therapy with apatinib mesylate combined with retlirafusp alfa injection until their disease progresses or they experience intolerable side effects.

After enrollment, participants will undergo safety visits before each dose on Day 1 and Day 21 of each treatment cycle. Tumor imaging assessments will be performed before treatment and after every 2 to 4 cycles of treatment. Clinical response will be evaluated by radiologists according to the RECIST 1.1 criteria.

Researchers will monitor participants for any adverse events throughout the study and will grade the severity of these events according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0. After treatment is completed, participants will be followed for 12 weeks for safety monitoring, and long-term survival follow-up will continue.
title: A Phase II Study of Nab-Paclitaxel Combined With Retlirafusp Alfa and Apatinib in Patients With Advanced Mucosal Melanoma

brief_summary: The present study aims to determine the effects of an XR-supported exercise education video developed for patients undergoing thoracic surgery on shoulder pain, range of motion (ROM), pulmonary function, quality of recovery, and adherence to the exercise program. This study is designed as a prospective, two-arm (1:1), randomized controlled clinical trial. The study population will consist of patients undergoing thoracic surgery at the Thoracic Surgery Clinic of Mersin University Hospital between October 2026 and October 2027. As shoulder pain is the primary outcome of the study, the sample size calculation was based on the study by Reeve et al. (2010). According to the a priori power analysis performed using G\*Power version 3.1, assuming a significance level of ? = 0.05, 95% statistical power (1?ß), and a two-tailed hypothesis, the required total sample size was calculated to be 54 patients. Considering a potential attrition rate of 10%, the target sample size was increased to 60 patients (30 in the XR-supported exercise education group and 30 in the control group). Data will be collected using the Patient Information Form, Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Range of Motion Assessment Form, Pulmonary Function Test Parameters Follow-up Form, Quality of Recovery-40 Questionnaire (QoR-40), and the Exercise Follow-up Form. Upon hospital admission, all participants will complete the Patient Information Form, Visual Analog Scale, Range of Motion Assessment Form, and Pulmonary Function Test Parameters Follow-up Form. Patients assigned to the intervention group will receive XR-supported exercise education before thoracic surgery, whereas those in the control group will receive the routine education provided in the clinic (consisting of verbal instruction and standard face-to-face patient education with demonstration). Participants in both the intervention and control groups will be assessed on postoperative days 7 and 14 using the Visual Analog Scale, Range of Motion Assessment Form, Pulmonary Function Test Parameters Follow-up Form, and the Quality of Recovery40 Questionnaire. During hospitalization, adherence to the prescribed exercise program will be monitored using the Exercise Follow-up Form based on patients' self-reports.
title: Effect of Extended Reality-Supported Exercise Training on Shoulder Pain, Range of Motion, Pulmonary Function, Quality of Recovery, and Adherence to the Exercise Program in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Curi01, a powder made of silica (silicon dioxide) particles, helps chronic, oozing diabetic foot ulcers heal when it is added to standard wound care. Curi01 is sprinkled directly onto the wound, where it soaks up wound fluid and forms a gel that is washed off at the next dressing change.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Do more wounds heal completely within 12 weeks when Curi01 is added to standard wound care, compared with standard wound care alone? A wound counts as healed when it is fully closed and still closed 14 days later.

Is Curi01 safe and well tolerated?

Researchers will compare Curi01 plus standard wound care to standard wound care alone. Standard wound care includes removing dead tissue, cleaning the wound, non-medicated dressings and pressure relief for the foot if applicable.

Participants will:

Be adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who have an oozing foot ulcer (2 to 10 cm²) that has been present for at least 6 weeks and has not improved enough with standard wound care First receive standard wound care for 2 weeks to check whether the wound improves on its own Then be assigned by chance to one of the two groups; 2 out of 3 participants will receive Curi01 Visit the study site up to 18 times over about 14 weeks; in the Curi01 group, the powder is applied at each visit until the wound is dry Have their wound photographed and measured with a wound imaging app at each visit Answer questionnaires about their quality of life and how they feel their condition has changed Be asked about any side effects or health problems

About 280 participants will take part at around 20 study sites in Germany. Participants and doctors will know which treatment is being given.
conditions: Foot Ulcer Due to Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
Foot Ulcer Due to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Healed Target Wound at Day 84
title: Silica-Based Wound Treatment (Curi01) Plus Standard Care Versus Standard Care Alone for Chronic Diabetic Foot Wounds

brief_summary:
Poor oocyte (egg before maturation) quality remains a major barrier to IVF success, particularly in women with prior cycles demonstrating low oocyte maturity, poor fertilization rates, or suboptimal embryo development. Preclinical and early clinical evidence suggests that the mTOR pathway plays a critical role in oocyte and follicular development, and pharmacologic inhibition with sirolimus (also known as rapamycin), may improve oocyte competence by adjusting granulosa cell function and follicular aging processes.

We propose a multicenter pilot study enrolling participants at the Center for Human Reproduction (CHR) in New York and at the Division of Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. Participants will be aged 20-45 years with a documented history of poor oocyte quality in at least one prior IVF cycle, defined by low oocyte maturity (\<50%), low IVM rates (\<50%), poor fertilization (\<70%), or suboptimal embryo quality (\<50% cleavage-stage embryos or no embryos graded B4 or higher), despite normal ovarian response for age and reserve. After enrollment, participants will undergo ovarian priming with Sirolimus 1 mg orally daily in late luteal phase (from cycle-day 19-21 until menstrual period, hence for a total of 7-10 days), immediately preceding ovarian stimulation for embryo banking and later embryo transfer (after at least 12 weeks).

The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary efficacy of short-term sirolimus treatment for cycle priming prior to IVF, with the goal of improving oocyte quality and developmental competence. The main outcome will be embryo quality compared with historical cycles, although other secondary outcomes derived from egg quality will be assessed.
primary_outcomes: Responder vs. non-responder to rapamycin priming
title: Effect of Sirolimus on Oocyte Quality in Women Undergoing IVF

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to understand why some adults continue to test positive for chlamydia or gonorrhea after receiving antibiotic treatment.

The study will also explore whether sexual health knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and practices are linked to positive test results after treatment.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

How many participants test positive for chlamydia or gonorrhea four or eight weeks after treatment? Are differences in sexual health knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and practices linked to positive test results? Are treatment adherence and sexual behaviors after treatment linked to positive test results? The study will include 238 adults diagnosed with chlamydia, gonorrhea, or both infections at the Centre Hospitalier de Martigues in France.

Participants will:

Receive standard antibiotic treatment as part of their usual medical care. Answer a questionnaire about their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and practices.

Attend two follow-up visits, approximately four and eight weeks after their initial visit.

Provide samples for additional laboratory tests to check for chlamydia or gonorrhea at both follow-up visits.

Answer questions about their treatment and sexual behaviors during follow-up. The researchers will compare participants who test positive after treatment with those who test negative. This comparison may help identify factors linked to persistent infection or a new infection.

Participation is voluntary. The study does not involve experimental medication or changes to the usual antibiotic treatment.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With a Positive Post-Treatment NAAT/PCR Test at Week 4 and/or Week 8
