brief_summary:
A prospective cohort study with patients undergoing surgery at the Neurosurgery Clinic of the University Clinical Hospital Mostar.

Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria: Inclusion criteria will be: a) patients over 18 years of age undergoing elective surgery for degenerative spine diseases b) ASA status 1-3 Exclusion criteria will be: a) emergency surgeries b) spinal trauma c) allergy to any of the drugs routinely administered during surgery (cefazolin, pantoprazole, metoclopramide, sevoflurane, propofol, fentanyl) d) patients under 18 years of age e) ASA status 4 Variables and Data Sources: General patient data will be collected (gender, age, height, weight), comorbidities, and baseline values for hemoglobin, hematocrit, leukocytes, C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin 6 (IL-6), ferritin, blood glucose (BG), creatine kinase, myoglobin, and cholesterol. These values will be monitored on the first and second postoperative days, and the dynamics of the results will be recorded. Intraoperatively, the need for vasopressors and transfusions will be documented, and the occurrence of postoperative infections, as well as postoperative nausea and vomiting, will be monitored.
title: Comparison of the Inflammatory Response in Patients Undergoing Surgery for Degenerative Spinal Diseases: Sevoflurane-Based Balanced Anesthesia Versus Target-Controlled Propofol Infusion (TCI)

brief_summary: Patients often encounter unpleasant sore throat after surgery when wake up from general anaesthesia and pulling off breathing tube. Lignocaine is a medication used in anaesthesia for the properties of analgesia and anti-inflammation. Other studies suggested that lignocaine spray/ gel can reduce the postoperative sore throat after extubation in patients undergoing surgery. However, it can reduce the gag reflex, resulting in higher risk of aspiration after surgery. Therefore, this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial is designed to determine whether giving intravenous lignocaine toward the end of the surgery before extubation can reduce postoperative sore throat and discomfort after surgery. It is hypothesized that intravenous lignocaine can reduce postoperative sore throat in patients undergoing general anaesthesia.
title: Intravenous LIGNOcaine for the POstoperative Sore Throat

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study was to learn if a mental health educational program can improve self-esteem and reduce stress and anxiety in school girls in Sana'a, Yemen.

The main question aims to answer:

Is there a significant difference in self-esteem, stress, and anxiety outcomes between the intervention group participating in the mental health educational program and the control group?

Participants will:

Complete self-reported questionnaires assessing self-esteem (RSES), stress (PSS-10), and anxiety (GAD-7) at baseline pre-test, immediate post-intervention post-test, and 3 months follow up post-test.

Attend interactive 5-days psychoeducational program sessions delivered within their school setting (intervention school), and 5-days placebo program for (control school).
title: Evaluating a School-based Mental Health Program on Self-esteem, Stress, and Anxiety Among Adolescent Girls in Yemen.

brief_summary: A prospective, randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted among patients with ARDS admitted to Ward 2 of the Neurosurgical Intensive Care Unit (ICU) between February and October 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to an experimental group or a control group using a random number table. Both groups received routine nursing care. The experimental group was managed using a 90° lateral positioning strategy, whereas the control group was managed using a 30° lateral positioning strategy. Differences between the two groups were compared in terms of vital signs, oxygenation index, Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS), gastric residual volume, intracranial pressure (ICP), cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP), mean duration of mechanical ventilation, mean ICU length of stay, duration of repositioning, and the incidence of complications.
title: Effect of 90-Degree Side Lying on Breathing in Neurocritical ARDS Patients

brief_summary:
Falls, reduced muscle strength, and balance problems are common among older adults and can affect their ability to perform daily activities independently. These difficulties may increase the risk of falling, limit mobility, and contribute to fear of falling and reduced psychological well-being. Regular muscle-strengthening and balance exercises may help older adults improve physical function, maintain independence, and increase confidence in everyday movement. Home-based exercise programs may provide an accessible and practical approach, particularly for individuals who have difficulty attending rehabilitation facilities.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured home-based muscle-strengthening and balance-training program in improving lower-limb functional performance, balance, and fear of falling among older adults. The study also examined changes in frailty, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. The researchers hypothesized that participants receiving the home-based exercise program would experience greater improvements in physical performance and balance, along with reduced fear of falling, compared with those continuing their usual activities.

This randomized controlled trial was conducted at Bangladesh Medical University (formerly Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University), Dhaka, Bangladesh. The study involved older adults aged 60-75 years with a history of recurrent falls and difficulties with balance or physical mobility. Participants were randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group.

Participants in the intervention group received a supervised home-based exercise program focusing on strengthening the muscles of the lower limbs and improving balance. Participants in the control group continued their usual daily activities and routine care without participating in the structured exercise program.

The researchers assessed balance using the Berg Balance Scale and lower-limb functional performance using the Five Times Sit-to-Stand Test, which measures how quickly a person can stand up from and sit down on a chair five times. Additional assessments measured frailty, fear of falling, anxiety, and depressive symptoms using standardized questionnaires.

Changes in these measures were compared between the two groups to determine whether home-based strengthening and balance exercises provided additional benefits beyond usual activities. The study aimed to generate evidence on the potential usefulness of home-based exercise as an accessible rehabilitation approach for improving physical function, balance, and well-being among older adults, particularly in settings with limited access to rehabilitation services.
primary_outcomes: Change in Functional Balance Assessed Using the Berg Balance Scale (BBS)
Change in Lower-Limb Functional Performance Assessed Using the Five Times Sit-to-Stand Test (5TSTS)
title: Home-Based Exercise and Improvements in Balance, Physical Function, and Fear of Falling Among Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Pain after minimally invasive cardiac surgery can affect breathing, movement, and recovery. Regional anesthesia techniques may help reduce postoperative pain and the need for opioid pain medications.

This study aims to compare two ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia approaches for pain management after minimally invasive cardiac surgery: erector spinae plane block (ESPB) and a combination of parasternal intercostal plane block (PIPB) and rhomboid intercostal block (RIB).

A total of 56 adult patients undergoing minimally invasive cardiac surgery will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive ESPB, while the other group will receive the combined PIPB and RIB technique. Both approaches will use the same total dose of local anesthetic and will be performed after induction of general anesthesia and before surgery.

The main objective is to compare how pain scores at rest change between the two groups during the first 12 hours after removal of the breathing tube. Pain will be assessed using a numerical scale from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable pain).

The study will also evaluate postoperative opioid consumption, additional pain measurements, quality of recovery, and block-related adverse events. Quality of recovery will be assessed using the QoR-15T questionnaire before surgery and 48 hours after extubation.Patient-reported acceptability of postoperative pain management will also be evaluated using a Likert scale at 48 hours postoperatively.

The findings may help identify effective regional anesthesia strategies for postoperative pain management in minimally invasive cardiac surgery.
interventions: Combined Parasternal Intercostal Plane Block (PIPB) and Rhomboid Intercostal Block (RIB)
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Resting Pain Scores Assessed by the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS)
title: ESPB Versus Combined PIPB and RIB for Analgesia in Minimally Invasive Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary: Flexible cystoscopy is an examination of the urethra and bladder performed with a flexible instrument under local anesthesia. Patients may experience pain and anxiety during the examination. This randomized study compares listening to patient-preferred music, conversation with the urologist, and routine care in men undergoing flexible cystoscopy. The main outcomes are pain and anxiety associated with flexible cystoscopy, assessed using a visual analog scale and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory State subscale, respectively. Other assessments include pain at specific stages of the procedure, anxiety on a visual analog scale, blood pressure and pulse changes, patient satisfaction, willingness to undergo the procedure again, and procedure duration.
title: Music and Conversation for Pain and Anxiety During Flexible Cystoscopy

brief_summary: Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) is a chronic neuropathic pain syndrome suffered by patients with herpes zoster and often adversely affect patients' normal lives, leading to declines in sleep and quality of life. Ketamine/esketamine has been used for treatment of chronic pain but may produce adverse psychiatric reactions at slightly higher doses, including dissociative symptoms, hallucinations, and nightmares; the sedative effect of dexmedetomidine helps mitigate its psychiatric side effects. A previous study in orthopedic surgery patients also showed that dexmedetomidine combined with esketamine can significantly improve perioperative analgesia and sleep quality. The investigators hypothesize that intranasal administration of dexmedetomidine combined with esketamine in patients with postherpetic neuralgia can improve analgesic efficacy.
primary_outcomes: Sum of pain intensity difference (SPID) within 7 days after the first administration
title: Intranasal Esketamine-dexmedetomidine Combination in Patients With Postherpetic Neuralgia

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of stress ball use on stress and anxiety levels in mothers who visit a family health center to have their infants vaccinated. The study will address the following questions:

* Does using a stress ball reduce mothers' stress levels?
* Does using a stress ball reduce mothers' anxiety levels? The researchers will compare the stress ball intervention with the control group. Participants will be assigned to the intervention and control groups in a 1:1 ratio using a computer-generated random number list. Group assignments will be kept in sealed, numbered envelopes.

Participants will:

* Be recruited from among mothers who visit Elazığ İzzetpaşa No. 1 Family Health Center to have their infants receive routine vaccinations and who meet the study's eligibility criteria.
* Include approximately 72 mothers (36 in the intervention group and 36 in the control group).
* Receive the stress ball intervention if assigned to the intervention group. The control group will receive the control procedure described in the study protocol.
* Have their stress and anxiety levels assessed using the measurement instruments specified in the protocol.
primary_outcomes: State-Trait Anxiety Inventory - State Anxiety Subscale (STAI Form TX-I)
title: Effect of a Stress Ball on Stress and Anxiety in Mothers Having Their Infants Vaccinated

brief_summary: This quasi-experimental study assessed a microclinics intervention designed to improve the nutritional status of children under two years on Mfangano Island, Kenya. The intervention, implemented in Mfangano East, involved six biweekly nutrition education sessions and action plans for mothers and caregivers. A total of 161 caregiver-child pairs from Mfangano East and the comparison community of Mfangano North participated in the study. Sociodemographic information, child anthropometry, dietary diversity and meal frequency were assessed at baseline and six months later.
primary_outcomes: Dietary Diversity; Percentage of Children Achieving Minimum Dietary Diversity Assessed by Caregiver-Reported 24-Hour Dietary Recall
title: Assessment of the Effects of Microclinics Intervention on Nutritional Status of Children Aged 6-23 Months in Mfangano Island, Western Kenya

brief_summary: Anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a rare malignancy, accounting for only 2.5% of gastrointestinal tumours. For patients with early-stage disease , concurrent chemoradiotherapy (fluorouracil/mitomycin combined with radiotherapy) achieves a 5-year survival rate of 60%-80%, whereas the prognosis deteriorates markedly for patients with advanced and metastatic disease. More effective therapeutic regimens are therefore urgently needed for advanced patients to prolong survival. EGFR positivity is frequently observed in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, and anti-EGFR targeted therapy as well as immunotherapy have demonstrated favourable efficacy in advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. This study aims to explore the efficacy of the PD-1 inhibitor putelimab in combination with the EGFR-targeted ADC MRG003 as second-line treatment for patients with advanced anal squamous cell carcinoma.
title: Radiotherapy Plus Putelimab and Vibostolimab for Advanced Anal Squamous Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary: This study looks at two different surgical techniques used during lung surgery (upper lobectomy). Surgeons may either divide or preserve a thin tissue band called the pulmonary ligament. The investigators want to understand how this choice affects recovery, including changes in lung size, airway shape, and symptoms such as cough. Forty patients took part, with half receiving ligament division and the other half with ligament preservation post upper lobectomy. Lung volume and airway changes were measured using CT scans, and cough scores were recorded after surgery. The study also noted one patient in the division group who developed a space problem (pneumothorax) two weeks after surgery. The goal is to learn which approach may help patients recover more comfortably and reduce postoperative symptoms.
interventions: Upper lobectomy with pulmonary ligament division
title: Pulmonary Ligament Division vs Preservation in Upper Lobectomy

brief_summary: This Phase II clinical trial protocol will provide evidence as to whether IN insulin is efficacious in reducing symptoms in people seeking care for mild TBI (concussion).
primary_outcomes: Change in Post-Concussion Symptom Scale scores (PCSS) from baseline to 21 days

brief_summary:
Chronic ankle instability is a common condition that can affect balance, movement control, and daily activities in young adults. Breathing exercises may influence brain function and attention, but their immediate effects on brain activity in individuals with chronic ankle instability are not well understood.

This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the immediate effects of different breathing interventions on brain activity in young adults with chronic ankle instability. Participants will be randomly assigned to different breathing intervention groups. Brain activity will be assessed before and after the intervention using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and electroencephalography (EEG). The findings may improve understanding of the relationship between breathing exercises and brain function and support the development of rehabilitation strategies for individuals with chronic ankle instability.

Change in frontopolar cortex oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO2) concentration measured by fNIRS
Change in orbitofrontal cortex oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO2) concentration measured by fNIRS
Change in medial prefrontal cortex oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO2) concentration measured by fNIRS

Change in EEG theta band power
Change in EEG alpha band power

title: How Different Breathing Methods Affect Brain Activity in Young Adults With Chronic Ankle Instability

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the effects of a virtual reality (VR) multidomain intervention on cognitive function in older adults with cognitive frailty and explore its underlying mechanisms.Participants will receive either supervised VR training twice weekly for 24 weeks or multidomain health education. The VR program combines cognitive training, physical exercise, nutrition education, and emotional support.Cognitive function, physical function, emotional symptoms, and nutritional status will be assessed at baseline and Week 24. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy will assess brain activity to explore potential mechanisms. Intervention feasibility, acceptability, and safety will also be evaluated.
title: Multidomain Virtual Reality Training for Older Adults Living With Cognitive Frailty

brief_summary:
The goal of this quasi-experimental study is to determine if there are improved outcomes for patients with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) who walk daily. The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Are patients with PPROM who walk at least 3500 steps per day more likely to stay pregnant longer than those who walk less?

Participants will be encouraged to walk ≥3500 steps per day from the time of diagnosis until delivery and their daily step counts will be recorded. Researchers will compare those who actually walk ≥3500 steps per day to those who walk less.
title: Steps to Extend Latency in Preterm Prelabor Rupture of Membranes

brief_summary:
This ongoing, single-group pilot feasibility study aims to evaluate the feasibility, usability, and acceptability of an occupation-based immersive virtual reality (IVR) rehabilitation program for adults with stroke-related upper-limb impairment. The study has an anticipated enrollment of 20 participants, of whom eight were enrolled during the initial recruitment period.

The intervention consists of 12 supervised sessions per participant, each including approximately 30 minutes of virtual activities delivered through two custom-developed IVR applications, Virtual Gardening and Virtual Painting, using a Meta Quest 2 head-mounted display (HMD). The intervention is provided as an adjunct to usual occupational therapy.

The study examines intervention completion, session delivery, gameplay duration, technical interruptions, safety, user satisfaction, symptoms associated with virtual reality exposure, and participation during rehabilitation sessions. Upper-limb motor function and independence in activities of daily living are also assessed as exploratory clinical outcomes.

The primary aim is to determine whether this occupation-based IVR rehabilitation program can be feasibly implemented in clinical practice and to identify areas for improvement before larger-scale studies. The study is not designed to establish the effectiveness of the intervention compared with conventional rehabilitation.
title: Feasibility of Occupation-Based Immersive Virtual Reality for Upper-Limb Rehabilitation After Stroke

brief_summary:
Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome (GTPS) is a common musculoskeletal condition associated with lateral hip pain, impaired muscle function, and reduced physical performance. This randomized controlled trial aims to investigate the effects of motor control exercises combined with myofascial release techniques on pain intensity, pain threshold, muscle activation patterns, muscle strength, functional capacity, quality of life, and gait parameters in individuals diagnosed with GTPS.

A total of 72 participants with GTPS will be randomly allocated to one of three groups: (1) motor control exercises combined with myofascial release techniques, (2) motor control exercises alone, or (3) a control group receiving a home-based motor control exercise program in brochure format. Outcome measures will be assessed at baseline and after an 8-week intervention period. The results of this study may provide evidence for optimizing rehabilitation strategies for individuals with GTPS.
primary_outcomes: Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire -Pain Rating Index
Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire - Present Pain Intensity
Short-Form McGill Pain Questionnaire - Visual Analog Scale
title: Motor Control Exercise and Myofascial Release in Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome

brief_summary: This study aims to implement a rigorously standardized protocol to investigate the effect of acute (60 min prior) caffeine intake or hypoxia (1000m and 2000m) on 4km time trial performance.
title: Effects of Hypoxia or Caffeine on 4km Time-trial Morning Cycling.

brief_summary:
Our proposed project will seek to determine if an oral medication called zileuton, which blocks the synthesis of inflammatory molecules called leukotrienes that are involved in allergic reactions, may be able to decrease absorption of food allergens and prevent severe food allergy reactions from occurring. Our study will measure levels of peanut in the blood before and after subjects consume an allergen they can tolerate and compare the results with and without administration of the study medication, zileuton. If our study shows that zileuton can decrease the absorption of a food allergen, this will allow us to see if this medication can be used to prevent anaphylaxis to food.

The goal of this proof-of-concept study is to determine whether zileuton inhibits food allergen absorption in children and adolescents with food allergy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does zileuton administration impact food allergen absorption in children and adolescents with food allergies?
* What is the variability of food allergen absorption in children and adolescents with IgE-mediated food allergies?

Researchers will compare levels of peanut allergen proteins in the participants' blood with and without a dose of zileuton prior to a test meal of peanut protein.

* Visit 1 will involve a baseline blood draw, a test meal of peanut protein and a post-meal blood draw.
* Visit 2 will involve a baseline blood draw, a dose of zileuton before the test meal of peanut protein, and blood draws after the test meal.
primary_outcomes: Inhibition of food allergy absorption by zileuton
title: Zileuton for Food Allergy

Chronic pain is one of the common postoperative complications in major surgery patients, which seriously affects the prognosis of patients. The postoperative pain level in spinal cord surgery patients is severe, and the incidence of CPSP can be as high as 40%.

Prolonged multimodal analgesia strategies using non-opioid or low-opioid receptor agonists can safely extend the postoperative pain window to one month, thereby further avoiding the occurrence of chronic postoperative pain.

This study provides guidance for perioperative pain management strategies in spinal surgery patients and further improves their long-term prognosis and outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of moderate-to-severe chronic pain at 3 months postoperatively
title: Prolonged Multimodal Analgesia for Postsurgical Pain

brief_summary:
Background/Objectives: Polyethylene glycol 3350 (PEG), monobasic sodium phosphate (NaP) and sennoside A+B calcium (Senna) are among the most commonly used bowel preparation agents, and numerous studies have been conducted regarding their efficacy and adverse effects. However, the data comparing their effects on oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory responses at both systemic and intestinal mucosal levels are limited. Considering the potential harmful effects of oxidative stress-induced DNA damage and inflammation, the biochemical side effects of bowel cleansing agents should also be investigated in terms of oxidative stress and inflammation.

Methods: Approximately 90 patients will be randomly assigned to receive PEG, NaP, or Senna for bowel preparation. Planned 30 patients for each solution groups will be the main arms of the study.

Venous blood samples will be collected before and after bowel preparation usage, and sigmoid colon mucosal biopsies will be taken. Both serum and colonic mucosal total antioxidant status (TAS) and total oxidant status (TOS) levels will be measured. Oxidative stress index (OSI) is also going to be calculated. Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels will also be measured. Changes in serum parameters will be expressed as delta (Δ) values. A biochemical analysis was planned to determine which solution induced more oxidative stress and inflammation in serum and colonic mucosal tissue. We believe , this will be an important comparison in terms of the biochemical safety of the solutions.
interventions: Colon preparation for colonoscopy (FLEET PHOSPHO-SODA 45ml ®) Recordati, USA
Colon preparation for colonoscopy X-M DİET 250 mL ®, Avixa, Turkey
Colon preparation for colonoscopy (PEGDIN POWDER ®. DİNÇSA, Turkey)
primary_outcomes: Serum delta (Δ) values of IL-6, TAS, TOS or OSI among the solution groups
Tissue TAS, TOS and OSI levels of the sigmoid colon among the solution groups
Correlations between serum IL-6 levels and oxidative stress parameters.
title: Comparison of the Effects of PEG, Sodium Phosphate and Sennoside A+B Calcium Bowel Preparations on IL-6 Levels and Oxidative Stress Markers: A Prospective Randomized Study
